meta.description: End-to-end pooled and single-cell CRISPR screen analysis from FASTQ to hit genes: library QC, guide counting, six-stage screen QC, method-matched hit calling across MAGeCK/BAGEL2/drugZ/JACKS/Chronos, copy-number and batch correction, and tier-based cross-method consensus, with branches to editing/single-cell/in-vivo variants.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, statistics, or trial data; all citations in the References section are real and correctly attributed.

practice_boundaries.detail: Scope is experimental/technical screen diagnostics throughout; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about human subjects.

methodological_ground.detail: Step 3's shipped 'Replicate Pearson' QC code averages the full pairwise correlation matrix, conflating true replicate pairs with baseline-vs-endpoint pairs. On real HAP1 TKOv3 data this understates true replicate concordance (0.677 naive vs 0.789 true T18-replicate-only), straddling the workflow's own 0.8/0.85 QC gate -- a principled statistical conflation, not a stylistic issue.

code_usability.detail: Every code block runs when given internally-consistent inputs (MAGeCK RRA, BAGEL2 fc/bf, drugZ, Step 7 tier-consensus merge, JACKS CLI flags, Chronos API calls all verified against real installs); the Step 2/Step 6a sample-label mismatch is a cross-example inconsistency, not unrunnable code within a single block.

functional_suitability.note: End-to-end coverage across 15 chained Skills is thorough and complete, but two real correctness defects were found in shipped code: the QC 'Replicate Pearson' formula conflates replicate and non-replicate sample pairs, and Step 2/Step 6a's own worked examples use incompatible sample-label schemes that error when composed in sequence.

reliability.note: The Common Errors table covers real, plausible failure symptoms, but does not cover the Step 2/6a sample-label mismatch or the BAGEL2 run-to-run non-determinism this audit reproduced; no recovery guidance exists for either.

performance_context.note: Token-efficient prose for the scope covered (15 chained sub-skills, 6 specialized branches); code blocks are concise, adapted patterns rather than verbose boilerplate.

agent_usability.note: Strong decision aids (Pipeline Branches diagram, Decision Cheat Sheet, Made-Once Commitments table) support learnability, but consistency is undermined by the CN-threshold drift between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md, and error prevention is weakened by the absence of a pre-flight gate for missing baseline/library/CN commitments.

human_usability.note: Quick Start and worked Example Prompts (including the exact Diagnostics scenario tested here) aid discoverability; forgiveness is limited since neither the sample-label mismatch nor the BAGEL2 determinism issue has documented recovery guidance.

security.note: No credential exposure, destructive operations, or prompt-injection vectors in any script or instruction.

maintainability.note: Well cross-referenced (15-entry Related Skills list, real DOIs in References), but the CN-bias residual-correlation gate is stated as <0.10 in SKILL.md's frontmatter and flatly <0.05 in usage-guide.md's cheat-sheet table -- a documentation-sync defect on a numeric pass/fail threshold.

agent_specific.note: Composability across chained sub-skills mostly works -- Step 7's tier-consensus code ran unmodified against real 3-method output -- but two adjacent worked examples (Step 2, Step 6a) don't compose without manual correction, and no escape hatch exists for missing made-once commitments before hit-calling proceeds.

recommendations.title: BAGEL2 non-determinism silently destabilizes the workflow's own Tier consensus
recommendations.problem: Running the SKILL.md's own documented BAGEL2 bf command twice on identical input produced materially different Bayes Factors (mean abs diff 1.31, max 89.3 across 18,053 genes); 39 genes flipped their bagel_hit (BF>6) classification between runs, changing their Tier in Step 7's consensus output.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md invokes BAGEL.py bf as a required consensus method (Steps 6a, 7) with no seed-management, run-averaging, or determinism caveat anywhere in the document.
recommendations.fix: Document BAGEL2's run-to-run BF variance explicitly; recommend averaging BF over multiple runs (or using BAGEL2's own bootstrap flag with a fixed, documented iteration count) before thresholding for Tier assignment.

recommendations.title: Shipped 'Replicate Pearson' QC formula conflates replicate and non-replicate sample pairs
recommendations.problem: Step 3's code averages ALL off-diagonal pairwise correlations, including baseline-vs-endpoint pairs. On real HAP1 TKOv3 data this gives 0.677, while the true endpoint-replicate correlation (T18A/B/C only) is 0.789 -- an 0.11 gap straddling the workflow's own stated 0.8/0.85 QC gate.
recommendations.root_cause: The code has no concept of which sample-pairs are true replicates vs different conditions/timepoints; it treats the full correlation matrix as homogeneous.
recommendations.fix: Compute replicate Pearson only over an explicitly declared replicate-group mapping (same-condition columns), not the full pairwise matrix that includes baseline-vs-endpoint comparisons.

recommendations.title: Step 2's and Step 6a's own worked examples don't compose
recommendations.problem: Following Step 2's drug-screen count command (sample-label Plasmid,Day0,Veh_r1,Veh_r2,Drug_r1,Drug_r2) directly into Step 6a's literal mageck test command (--treatment-id Day14_r1,Day14_r2,Day14_r3) produces a hard MAGeCK error because those columns don't exist in Step 2's output.
recommendations.root_cause: Step 6a's example uses a different (time-course-style) sample-label scheme than Step 2's example; a single caveat sentence flags the mismatch but never resolves it with matching commands for the scenario Step 2 actually walks through.
recommendations.fix: Give Step 6a a hit-calling example that uses Step 2's own sample labels (Veh_r*/Drug_r*), or clearly separate the two worked scenarios end-to-end with self-consistent counting and hit-calling commands for each.

recommendations.title: CN-bias QC threshold conflicts between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's frontmatter states the CN-bias gate as abs(rho)<0.10 ('<0.05 is a stricter target'), while usage-guide.md's QC Checkpoints table states flatly abs(rho)<0.05 as the pass criterion, so a screen with rho=0.07 passes by one document and fails by the other.
recommendations.root_cause: The same numeric gate was authored independently in two files without cross-checking.
recommendations.fix: State one canonical threshold in SKILL.md and have usage-guide.md's table reference or repeat it verbatim, including the same optional-stricter-target language.

recommendations.title: No operational gate enforces the Skill's own 'made-once commitments' principle
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's governing principle states that a wrong-but-silent baseline/library/CN commitment 'invalidates the endpoint with no error thrown,' but no numbered step instructs the agent to confirm these commitments (or ask the user) before computing LFCs or hits when they are unspecified.
recommendations.root_cause: The principle is documented narratively (prose warnings, a consequences table) but never translated into a procedural checklist or gate in the numbered pipeline steps.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit pre-flight step before Step 2: if baseline, library control classes (NTC/CEGv2/NEGv1), or CN profile (for cancer lines) are unspecified, ask the user before proceeding.

recommendations.title: Step 6a's example is mislabeled 'time-course dropout design' under a 'Two-condition essentiality' heading
recommendations.problem: The terminology collision with Step 6b's distinct 'time-course' (MLE) method risks an agent picking the wrong hit-calling method for a genuine multi-timepoint design.
recommendations.root_cause: Loose, reused wording across two different method sections of the same document.
recommendations.fix: Rename the caption to 'two-timepoint dropout design' or similar, reserving 'time-course' terminology for Step 6b only.
